links.passage: Tied to an effective soil water monitoring program, good design, and appropriate management practices, microirrigation can have an application efficiency of 95% or better without drought stress, and is now used on about 5% of the irrigated area in the United States [NASS, 2002], although on less than 1% worldwide.
reference_entries: National Agricultural Statistic Service (NASS) (2002), 2002 census of agriculture, 2003 farm and ranch irrigation survey, vol. 3, special studies part 1, U.S. Dep. of Agric., Washington, D.C. (Available at http://www.nass.usda.gov/Census/Create_Census_FRIS.jsp#top)

links.passage: High-frequency drip irrigation and other microirrigation methods have been shown to increase the yield and quality of fruit and vegetable crops through reduced water and nutrient stresses.
supporting_passages: Tied to an effective soil water monitoring program, good design, and appropriate management practices, microirrigation can have an application efficiency of 95% or better without drought stress, and is now used on about 5% of the irrigated area in the United States [NASS, 2002], although on less than 1% worldwide.
links.inference_note: The yield and quality claim for drip/microirrigation carries no citation itself; the only citation sits in the adjacent sentence (NASS, 2002), which is attached to the adoption-area statistic rather than the yield claim.
reference_entries: National Agricultural Statistic Service (NASS) (2002), 2002 census of agriculture, 2003 farm and ranch irrigation survey, vol. 3, special studies part 1, U.S. Dep. of Agric., Washington, D.C. (Available at http://www.nass.usda.gov/Census/Create_Census_FRIS.jsp#top)

links.passage: Microirrigation can be used over a wide range of terrain, and it has allowed expansion of irrigated crop production into areas with problem soils (either very low or very high infiltration rates), salt affected soils, and poor water quality that could not be utilized with other irrigation methods.
supporting_passages: It can be installed as either a surface [Schwankl and Hanson, 2007] or subsurface [Camp, 1998; Lamm and Camp, 2007] water application system.
links.inference_note: The claim that microirrigation has expanded irrigated crop production carries no citation itself; the citations sit in the adjacent sentence describing surface and subsurface drip installation.
links.citation_in_text: Schwankl and Hanson, 2007; Camp, 1998; Lamm and Camp, 2007
reference_entries: Schwankl, L. J., and B. R. Hanson (2007), Surface drip irrigation, in Microirrigation for Crop Production, edited by F. R. Lamm, J. E. Ayars, and F. S. Nakayama, chap. 12, pp. 431 – 472, Elsevier, New York.
